text: The procedure separates cheap proposal work from expensive target evaluation. A small proposer drafts five tokens sequentially, with each guess conditioned on its predecessors. The target then checks all five prefix positions concurrently in one round, so drafting still has a serial cost but target evaluation no longer requires a separate round for every position. A supplied correction rule retains the target distribution. On the toy workload, proposal work takes 4 ms, a target round takes 20 ms, and accepted yield averages three tokens. These measurements describe the evaluated token schedule rather than complete application latency.

text: A block-based cache changes how serving memory follows sequence growth. Logical token positions map to physical blocks that need not be adjacent, and another block is allocated only when an arriving token exhausts the current one. This permits incremental storage instead of reserving a contiguous region for the maximum sequence length. On the toy workload, the system supports a batch of 64 rather than 40 for contiguous reservation at the same 100 ms latency cap. That comparison concerns the evaluated allocation scheme; it does not isolate allocator overhead or establish a benefit on arbitrary hardware.
